reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm dasatinib engaged SRC kinases or bevacizumab engaged VEGFA. Target engagement must be inferred from clinical context only. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm kinase inhibition or angiogenesis modulation occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (PFS6) clearly missed - combination arm achieved 29% vs 18% for bevacizumab alone, difference of 11% with p=0.22, well above significance threshold. Effect size was modest and not statistically significant. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Study appears adequately powered (n=144), appropriate duration (156 weeks), and no major design flaws noted. This represents a clean efficacy failure where the combination hypothesis was tested but did not demonstrate benefit over bevacizumab monotherapy.

failure_modes.evidence: Primary endpoint missed with p=0.22 despite adequate sample size and duration. No biomarker data to confirm whether target engagement or pathway modulation occurred, but the failure to improve upon bevacizumab monotherapy suggests the combination hypothesis was not validated.
